title: Co-borrower liability disputes - the common misconceptions
p1:
Many people sign a loan as a co-borrower thinking they are only helping someone else. But one signature can create a responsibility they never expected.

A common belief is: “I didn’t use the money, so I don’t have to repay it.” That assumption can create serious problems.
p2:
The reality is different. A co-borrower is usually not just a witness or backup person. They share responsibility for the loan repayment. If the primary borrower stops paying, the lender may approach the co-borrower for recovery.

The surprising part? The lender generally does not have to first exhaust all options against the main borrower before seeking payment from the co-borrower.
p3:
Before becoming a co-borrower, people should carefully check the loan terms, repayment obligations, and long-term impact on their financial records. Helping a family member or friend is a personal decision, but it also creates a legal and financial commitment.

A signature on a loan document can carry much more weight than many people realize.
conclusion: Did you know a co-borrower can be held responsible even if they never received or used the loan amount? Share your thoughts or experiences.
